messages:
Sam R: quick question — when we dump the audit export for routing-policy rollouts, who is considered the canonical "actor"? the person who pushed the canary, the service account that did the deploy, or the author of the PR?
Julia K: we ran into this last week in the compliance review. right now exports include both `actor_id` (service account) and an optional `actor_hint` (git author), but not everyone knows which to trust.
Mike P: +1. ops wants a single primary field for linters/siem. can we adopt `actor_responsible` that picks precedence: explicit justification -> PR author -> deployer?
Lina: we need deterministic rules and a handoff checklist. if `actor_responsible` is derived, include `derivation_reason` in the export. otherwise auditors will ask us to prove chain of custody.
Sam R: agreed. proposal: export rows include `actor_responsible`, `actor_type` (human/service/bot), `derivation_reason` and a tiny verification blob `proof_hash`. `proof_hash` = sha256(tenant_id + change_id + actor_responsible + timestamp).
Julia K: love the `proof_hash` idea. makes it cheap to verify integrity without shipping large signed bundles. question: where do we store the secret salt for that hash? we can't put customer secrets in hosted logs.
Mike P: salt should be per-tenant in Private and Dedicated. for Hosted, we can publish the algorithm and include a `proof_link` (pre-signed, short TTL) that points to a verification endpoint controlled by us. auditors can follow link to confirm.
Lina: operational concern — pre-signed links add churn. can we include a signed JWT in the export instead? compact and self-contained.
Sam R: signed JWT works but requires KMS signing keys per environment/region. ops-bot: deploy-check: new env var `AUDIT_SIGNER_KEY_ID` must exist.
Mike P: tradeoffs noted. for MVP let's do: `actor_responsible`, `derivation_reason`, `proof_hash`, and `proof_link` (nullable). Implement JWT later.
Julia K: UX side — console must surface both `actor_responsible` and the fallback chain on the change details page. show a small badge: "verified" if `proof_link` succeeded in last 24h.
Lina: +1. Also add an export flag `--include-derivation` to the CLI so security teams can choose verbose vs compact dumps.
Sam R: follow-up actions: 1) eng-platform to add fields to audit schema (Mike), 2) console to show badge and chain (Julia), 3) ops to spec signer behavior for Dedicated/Private and hosted proof_link (Lina).
Mike P: I'll open a PR with schema patch and sample ndjson output. snippet:```{
  "change_id": "chg_2026_0001",
  "tenant_id": "tn_123",
  "actor_responsible": "julia.k",
  "actor_type": "human",
  "derivation_reason": "pr_author_fallback",
  "proof_hash": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...",
  "proof_link": "https://verif.redwood.ai/proofs/xxxxx?ttl=3600"
}```
Julia K: thanks. can we also add a tiny human-readable `assertion` field for audit exports so non-dev auditors can read one-liners? e.g., "Updated routing policy to pin tenant X to region us-east-1"
Sam R: yes, `assertion` added to the list.
Lina: ops note — we should rate-limit proof_link verification endpoints and include up-to-date logs for any verification failures. auditors will hit these a lot during investigations.
Mike P: noted. will add `verification_status` (enum: unknown/success/failure/expired) to the export record for convenience, populated after background check when available.
Julia K: timeline?
Sam R: target for schema PR + console prototype by end of next sprint. Mike will own PR, Julia will mock console changes, Lina will write ops runbook.
ops-bot: reminder created: /todo create runbook for audit proof signer — assignee Lina — due 7 days. :white_check_mark:
Mike P: thanks all — I'll draft the PR and ping reviewers.
Julia K: perfect. tagging @legal to keep them in the loop on what we'll surface to auditors.
Sam R: cool, thanks everyone. we'll reconvene if any blockers come up.
